news_boston.title: Airstrikes have paused and talks are pressing forward. But can the U.S. and Iran take the off-ramp?
news_boston.author: Ben Finley, Samy Magdy and Darlene Superville | The Associated Press
news_boston.summary:
The U.S. military has paused its airstrikes on Iran after nearly two weeks of intensifying bombing, while diplomatic efforts have pushed forward to try to avert a return to all-out war.

But it remains to be seen whether the U.S. and Iran are at an inflection point in a mercurial conflict that will reach the five-month point Tuesday. President Donald Trump both has threatened more strikes and said talks are pressing on, all while brushing off concerns that rising gas prices tied to the fighting could hurt Republicans in November’s midterm elections.

Adding to the uncertainty is the impact of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s planned visit with Trump next week in Washington. Israel, which launched the war alongside the U.S. on Feb. 28, has been notably absent from the renewed American attacks over Iran’s effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping corridor through which 20% of the world’s oil normally flows.

“The Iranians understand that perhaps it could get worse because Israel could come into the conflict,” said Michael Singh, managing director at the Washington Institute for Near East Policy. On the other hand, Israel’s lack of involvement so far “may signal to the Iranians that we’re looking to limit the conflict.”

Singh, who was senior Middle East director on the National Security Council during the George W. Bush administration, said he was hesitant to read too much into the lull in fighting.

“If it turns into a multiday pause, that’ll be something significant,” he said. “But it’s hard to know. Is it an operational pause? Is it a pause to allow for some kind of behind-the-scenes diplomacy?”

War with Iran Jul 24

House again passes a resolution seeking to halt military action in Iran as the conflict escalates

War with Iran Jul 23

Oil tankers attacked in the Red Sea as U.S.-Iran war widens and fuel prices spike

Mediators keep pressing their diplomatic efforts

A regional official involved in the mediation efforts said that concerted diplomacy was underway and that a pause in U.S. strikes and Iranian counterstrikes on neighboring countries hosting American forces was a “positive signal that helps their efforts to de-escalate.”

The official said that both the U.S. and Iran want to return to the interim ceasefire deal and that a compromise, which is being negotiated now, centers around having Iran run vessel transit through the Strait of Hormuz with fewer restrictions on ships. The official was not authorized to discuss the matter and spoke on condition of anonymity.

On Sunday, Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Esmail Baghaei, confirmed that Iran and Oman had held several rounds of technical talks about the strait in Iran over the weekend. He said that while the Omani delegation left Tehran on Saturday afternoon, talks had made progress and were continuing.

Iran put a chokehold on the narrow Persian Gulf waterway when the war began by firing on tankers and freighters. In turn, oil prices have soared during the conflict, which has been unpopular with many Americans, and could leave some Republican lawmakers vulnerable in November.

Following the signing of an interim ceasefire deal in June, a battle for control over the strait has erupted. Iran demanded that ships use a route near its coastline and said it can potentially charge fees. Ships were increasingly navigating a southern route along the coast of Oman under a U.S. overwatch operation when Iran attacked some vessels.

The U.S. renewed attacks on Iran’s coastal defenses, aiming to blunt Tehran’s ability to strike ships in the strait. The Trump administration then expanded its targets, hitting bridges and infrastructure in the south and striking deeper into the center of Iran.

Singh said the strikes appear to be an attempt to push Iran back to the negotiating table. Now, he said, “the question would be: What kind of messages, if any, is the Iranian regime sending through diplomatic channels? Have those messages changed? Do they seem more eager to return to talks?”

Among the challenges the U.S. faces is the fractured leadership in Iran, with different factions vying for control, Singh said, something that Trump administration officials have also pointed to. The people in charge in Iran may worry that compromising with the U.S. will be seen as weakness and could loosen their grip on power.

Whatever the case, both the U.S. and Iran need the strait to reopen for their own economic reasons.

“But they have very different conceptions of under what conditions, under whose control,” Singh said. “So we have to get to some kind of stable equilibrium on those questions before you’re going to see a longer period of quiet. I think this effort to negotiate with words and also to negotiate with force is going to continue until we reach that equilibrium.”

Trump issues threats but also talks up diplomacy

Despite the lull in fighting, tensions are high in the region.

Yemen’s Houthi rebels said Saturday that they fired missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia in response to Saudi airstrikes on the strategic Red Sea city of Hodeida. The Iran-backed rebels say they have closed the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which has become even more vital for Saudi oil exports since the disruption of the Strait of Hormuz.

The U.S. military also is enforcing its naval blockade of Iranian ports, saying it disabled a Mozambique-flagged ship in the Gulf of Oman on Friday after the vessel tried to violate the blockade and ignored warnings.

Trump also has kept up the threats against Iran even as he spotlighted diplomacy. Asked about his exit strategy Friday, Trump said there are two ways.

“You can just keep doing exactly what we’re doing and take them apart piece by piece. We could do it in a more rapid fashion, which we might do,” he told reporters in the Oval Office. “Or we can negotiate with them, which we’re also doing right now.”

While Trump said he doesn’t think Iran is “ready yet” to make a deal, he also asserted that “I think they’re getting more and more serious as the days go by, for maybe the obvious reason.”

Trump met Friday with top national security aides to discuss the situation with Iran and whether the administration should maintain the current course or escalate military attacks, according to a U.S. official who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss internal deliberations. No U.S. strikes occurred overnight in Iran after 13 consecutive nights.

Trump insisted Friday that he was “not in a hurry” to wrap things up because of the approaching elections, in which voters, angry about high food and gasoline prices, could vote his Republican Party out of control of Congress.

“Despite what everyone says about the election, I’m not in a hurry,” he said. “We have to do it right. Elections take care of themselves.”

____

Magdy reported from Cairo. Associated Press writer Matthew Lee contributed to this report.

news_boston.title: German police search for suspect in Berlin Pride van-ramming attack that left 1 dead, 16 injured
news_boston.author: Geir Moulson | The Associated Press
news_boston.summary:
German authorities on Sunday issued a wanted notice for a fugitive suspect in the van ramming near Berlin’s Pride festival that left one person dead and injured at least 16 others.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz described what happened late Saturday evening as “an attack on our society.”

Police and prosecutors asked for help in finding the 21-year-old suspect, whom they identified as Abdul B. They said he is believed to have injured several people with a moving vehicle, and that one or more people apparently then left that vehicle. Several people were also apparently stabbed, they added.

Sunday’s notice warned the public to avoid “direct contact” with the suspect, saying that he may be armed and dangerous.

Police had said earlier that they had identified a suspect who has ties to Islamic groups in the German capital.

“The suspect is known to police. He is known to us as a member of Islamic circles here in Berlin, and our search for this person is proceeding at full speed,” police spokesperson Florian Nath said.

Nath added that investigators had no information on “his specific motives.”

According to police, a white van drove into the Tiergarten park around 10 p.m. and hit several people before colliding with a tree. The closing party at the Pride festival, known as Christopher Street Day, was ongoing nearby at the time, following a parade with some 80 trucks that had made its way through downtown Berlin earlier in the day.

Police said a woman was killed. Berlin’s fire service said that three people sustained life-threatening injuries, another eight were seriously injured and five had slight injuries.

The Pride event next to the Brandenburg Gate was called off around 10:15 p.m. and a band’s performance on stage was interrupted. People were urged to go home and to avoid taking the route through the park.

“What an abhorrent act in Berlin,” Merz wrote in a post on X. He added that Germany loves freedom, “and we will preserve and defend that.”

Hundreds of thousands of people had come to Berlin to celebrate on Saturday, though it’s unclear how many were still at the festival by late evening. It’s one of Europe’s largest LGBTQ+ celebrations.

Julian Miethig, who had attended the party at the Brandenburg Gate, said he wanted to go to an afterparty when he heard from a friend that “something bad happened there and there are a lot of fire trucks, a lot of emergency vehicles, ambulances.”

“It’s a dark day for the community,” he said.

The van, with its battered front resting against a tree, could still be seen at the scene Sunday morning.

___

Associated Press writers Kirsten Grieshaber and Fanny Brodersen in Berlin contributed to this report.

news_boston.title: Red Sox trade Connelly Early for infielder Curtis Mead: Report
news_boston.author: Michael Hurley
news_boston.summary:
The Red Sox have made their first big move of the summer.

Boston traded left-handed pitcher Connelly Early to the Washington Nationals on Saturday night, receiving infielder Curtis Mead in return.

ESPN’s Jeff Passan broke the news.

Early has been on the injured list since July 1 due to elbow inflammation but is nearing a return to the mound. The 24-year-old made his MLB debut late last season with the Red Sox, and he ended up starting Game 3 of the Wild Card Series in Yankee Stadium.

Mead, 25, has primarily played at third base but has also played at second and first base.

The right-handed hitter is batting .256 with an .856 OPS this season, with 17 doubles and 17 home runs. In his career with the Rays, White Sox and Nationals, he’s a .245 hitter with a .710 OPS.

A native of Australia, Mead first entered professional baseball in the Phillies organization but was traded to the Rays for Cristopher Sanchez in 2019. The Rays traded Mead to the White Sox last year ahead of the deadline. The White Sox, though, designated Mead for assignment in March, eventually working out a trade that sent him to the Nationals.

The deal involves two controllable assets, as Early will be under team control until 2032 and Mead won’t reach free agency until 2031.

The deal for Craig Breslow was seemingly one made with a hope to bolster the offense, while giving up a piece of what has been an excellent and deep pitching staff. The rapid rise of rookie Jake Bennett (6-3, 2.58 ERA) along with the presence of fellow lefties Ranger Suarez, Payton Tolle and injured ace Garrett Crochet likely made the front office comfortable in dealing away Early.

The move came hours after the Red Sox mustered just one hit against Dylan Cease in a loss at Fenway Park, Boston’s fifth time being shut out this season. With Caleb Durbin turning his season around, Mead’s most obvious fit with Boston may be at second base, which has been a revolving door for the Red Sox this season. Marcelo Mayer started 39 games at second before moving to shortstop and subsequently hitting the IL. Veteran Isian Kiner-Filefa is also on the IL. Anthony Seigler has filled in admirably over the past month, but the trade signals the front office’s lack of belief that the 27-year-old with limited MLB experience can sustain his success.

All of Boston’s second basemen have combined for a .640 OPS this season, the fifth-worst mark in the majors.

The move certainly comes with risk, as Early has shown plenty of promise in his 21 big league appearances. Since debuting last September, Early has gone 8-7 with a 3.24 ERA and a 1.225 WHIP.

Despite Saturday’s loss, the Red Sox remained in the second wild card spot by the end of the day, a half-game up on the Guardians, who have a two-game cushion over the Twins in the third spot. Breslow is expected to continue to work to bolster the offense with a little more than a week remaining before the Aug. 3 trade deadline.

news_boston.title: Jetting off for a summer vacation? How to eat and drink to minimize jet lag
news_boston.author: Laura Ungar | The Associated Press
news_boston.summary:
Jet lag threatens to turn even a dream vacation into a slog.

And with peak travel season underway, millions of people may have to contend with this disorienting condition, which can cause sleep disturbances, daytime tiredness, headaches and nasty gastrointestinal symptoms.

But you can minimize the effects of jet lag — and not just by adjusting your sleep-wake schedule. What and how you eat and drink can make a difference too.

Jet lag occurs when your body’s biological clock is out of sync with the time zone you find yourself in. Usually, environmental cues such as sunrises and sunsets help set your internal clock. But when you cross time zones, it may take a few days for your body to adjust.

“I’ve personally experienced pretty severe jet lag before,” during two European trips, said Tara Schmidt, a registered dietitian at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. “It really kind of ruined the first few days of my vacation.”

Eat on the local schedule at your destination

While symptoms of jet lag vary, digestive problems such as bloating, constipation or diarrhea are not uncommon, said Joanne Slavin, a nutrition expert at the University of Minnesota, Twin Cities.

One way to minimize jet lag is to begin gradually shifting the timing of your meals as you get ready for travel. Schmidt suggested first moving them by 15 minutes, then a half hour, then an hour closer to the destination time zone.

World Cup Jul 19

The flight hours and miles of World Cup travels of FIFA's Infantino in numbers

Travel Jul 4

Small businesses say they're having a good summer as Americans travel closer to home

Then, after you get where you’re going, eat when the locals eat.

If it’s morning, have breakfast. A hearty one aligned with your new time zone can help you recover from jet lag, a 2023 study co-authored by Northwestern University researchers suggests.

As the day goes on, keep to the same schedule, having lunch and dinner at times appropriate for the location.

“Immediately go on your new schedule,” Slavin said.

To avoid stomachaches, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention advises keeping meals smaller just before and during travel. Schmidt said this is particularly important in the early days of a trip.

“Smaller meals tend to be more easily tolerated for people, especially if you have a sensitive stomach or maybe are dealing with some of those GI discomforts,” Schmidt said.

Later in the trip, she said, you may be able to ease into eating more at one sitting. Just be mindful about foods that you might not be used to, especially greasy or high-fat items.

“Enjoying a meal abroad is so fun, especially when you’re experiencing a new culture, a new food,” she said.

Watch what you drink on vacation

It’s also best to skip that glass of wine or pint of beer.

“As fun as it is sometimes when we travel, we really do endorse avoiding alcohol because alcohol is such a huge sleep disruptor,” Schmidt said.

Another pro tip: Use caffeine strategically. If you normally have a cup of coffee or tea in the morning, it’s fine to do that while traveling. But don’t have caffeine so late in the day that it will keep you up. And be aware that both caffeine and alcohol can make you more dehydrated.

“Dehydration can certainly worsen fatigue and those perceived jet lag symptoms,” Schmidt said.

Drink water before, during and after your flight to combat the effects of dry cabin air. At your destination, eight glasses of water a day is a good, easy-to-remember goal, but keep in mind that some people may need more fluids, others less, depending on things like weather and exercise. Cleveland Clinic experts suggest choosing bottled water if you have any questions about water safety.

When the trip is over, get back to your normal schedule

Experts say how and what you consume while traveling is only part of the equation for minimizing jet lag. But these changes complement the better known tips for adjusting your sleep schedule to the new time zone.

When your vacation begins winding down, the advice is much the same for sleep and eating: Ease back into your normal schedule and try to fully resume it at home.

“The sooner you get back to it, to all of your habits,” Slavin said, “the better off you’re going to be.”

State and local police are investigating a reported drowning at a quarry in Milford, Massachusetts, Saturday evening.

Information is extremely limited at this time, however, the Worcester County District Attorney’s Office confirmed the Milford Police Department and Massachusetts State Police detectives are investigating the incident, and aerial video from the scene showed there was a dive team in the water at the Milford Quarries.

Emergency crews were set up Sunday morning at the Shadowbrook Quarries, with the search for a missing swimmer set to resume.

Milford police have referred all further questions to the DA’s office, which said it is not releasing additional information at this time due to the ongoing investigation.

This incident comes just a few days after Milford police urged people to avoid the Shadowbrook Quarries after an 18-year-old fell from a rock ledge onto jagged rocks about 12 feet below and had to be flown by medical helicopter to UMass Memorial Medical Center for treatment Sunday night.

Police said the female victim was found conscious but bleeding from several areas while lying among broken bottles and leaves. She had no memory of the fall, and witnesses told police that she had briefly lost consciousness.

“While we’re thankful this incident did not have an even more tragic outcome, it serves as an important reminder that the Quarries are not a safe place for recreation. We continue to strongly discourage anyone from entering the property or swimming in the quarries,” police wrote on Facebook on Tuesday. “The steep rock faces, unstable terrain, and limited access for emergency responders create an extremely dangerous environment where a single misstep can have life-altering consequences for civilians and responders.”

news_boston.title: How digital evidence may be prosecution's backbone in D4vd's murder case
news_boston.author: Helen Jeong
news_boston.summary:
Nearly a year after the badly decomposed remains of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez were discovered in the front trunk of a black Tesla Model X, singer D4vd, whose legal name is David Anthony Burke, appeared in a downtown Los Angeles courtroom this week as prosecutors laid out their case accusing him of murdering and dismembering the teen.

The prosecution sought to convince Judge Charlaine F. Olmedo that probable cause existed to believe Burke committed the crime, presenting a series of findings from a modern digital homicide investigation — a fitting approach given the ages of both the Gen Z defendant and the alleged victim.

Burke’s text messages, cloud storage content, Amazon purchase history and Tesla data will likely be used against the 21-year-old based on what was presented during this week’s preliminary hearing.

Crime and Courts Jul 24

How photos, texts from D4vd's phone could shape the murder case

Crime and Courts Jul 23

Inflatable pool fragments, DNA samples from Tesla: New evidence in D4vd's pretrial hearing

Crime and Courts Jul 21

Judge hears evidence against singer D4vd in killing, dismemberment of teen to decide on trial

Amazon, Uber purchase history

On the first day of the preliminary hearing, prosecutors began discussing Burke’s purchases through Amazon and Uber Postmates, attempting to connect the singer to materials found among Rivas Hernandez’s remains.

The Amazon account was linked to a Gmail address that had been used to purchase United Airlines tickets for Burke and Rivas Hernandez.

Although the Amazon account was registered under the name Travion Davis, Burke confirmed in a Dec. 1, 2023, text message to Rivas Hernandez that he used the alias Travion Davis for “all (his) packages.”

Prosecutors alleged Burke used the Amazon account — and the alias — to purchase two orange-and-black electric chainsaws, two cadaver bags marketed as “morgue body bag Halloween 6′ long decoration prop(s)” and heavy-duty laundry bags.

A shovel and another chainsaw were delivered to Burke’s home through Uber Postmates using an account connected to him, according to Los Angeles Police Department Detective Josh Byers.

Prosecutors later argued that the purchased items matched those found in the garage of a Hollywood Hills home Burke had rented.

Data from Tesla X

A California Highway Patrol officer testified this week that a Caltrans worker found Rivas Hernandez’s passport ID card in a dirt turnout along Highway 154 in Santa Barbara County on Jan. 7, 2026.

A few days later, LAPD Detective William Roecker took the stand to explain the connection between Burke and the location where the passport ID card was found.

Roecker, who specializes in technology and cellular analysis, testified that cell tower data showed Burke’s Tesla Model X — the same vehicle in which Rivas Hernandez’s remains were later found — and the singer’s cellphone traveled together in April 2025 from his rented Hollywood Hills home to the Santa Barbara County location.

The detective said the data showed Burke’s Tesla and cellphone leaving the Hollywood Hills residence between 11 p.m. and 11:30 p.m. on April 23, 2025. The vehicle and cellphone then returned from Santa Barbara County between 4:03 a.m. and 7:07 a.m. on April 24, 2025, Roecker testified.

According to Roecker, Burke traveled to the same location several more times in May 2025. The detective said data from Burke’s Tesla and cellphone showed trips to and from the area on May 8, May 9 and May 31.

Sexually explicit photos

LAPD Detective Corey Farell, a nearly 30-year veteran of the department, took the stand Friday, describing the photos, videos and text messages he reviewed from Burke’s and Rivas Hernandez’s cellphones — key evidence in the prosecution’s argument that Burke sexually abused a minor.

Farell testified that the pair’s initial conversations began when Rivas Hernandez was 11 years old. Two years later, when she was an eighth-grader, their relationship became romantic, the detective said.

According to images presented by prosecutors, the relationship was sexual in nature.

The 13-year-old girl appeared in dozens of photos with the then-18-year-old man, including images in which she was nude and engaged in sexual activity, prosecutors alleged.

Some of the images also appeared to show the two exchanging explicit photographs, according to the prosecution.

The photos may support the prosecution’s claims that Burke stabbed Rivas Hernandez to death and attempted to cover up the crime to prevent their relationship from becoming public and jeopardizing his lucrative music career.

Eight-grader had an abortion

Detective Farrell testified that Rivas Hernandez began communicating with Burke on Aug. 8, 2022, when she was 11 years old. Their final recorded conversation occurred on April 23, 2025.

During the nearly three-year period, the two discussed plans to meet and communicated regularly by text message.

Farrell testified that investigators recovered messages referencing emergency contraceptives, including Plan B, as well as a photograph showing the pair posing with a box of the medication.

According to testimony, messages presented in court also included discussions that prosecutors argued were related to a possible pregnancy. In one exchange from January 2024, Burke apologized for “putting (her) through this,” and Rivas Hernandez responded that neither of them was capable of caring for a child.

Prosecutors also pointed to later messages that they argued referenced an abortion. According to messages shown in court, Burke offered what he described as an “abortion gift,” and Rivas Hernandez responded by requesting a designer handbag. In another exchange, prosecutors said Rivas Hernandez appeared to reference having undergone an abortion.

news_boston.title: Van slams into crowd at Berlin's Pride event, killing 1 and injuring 16, as police identify suspect
news_boston.author: Kirsten Grieshaber and Fanny Broderson | The Associated Press
news_boston.summary:
A van slammed into people gathered for Berlin’s famed Pride festival on Saturday night, killing one person, injuring at least 16 others and prompting police to call off the celebrations and a concert in the German capital hours after they had begun.

Berlin police said they have identified a suspect who has not been arrested and he has ties to Islamic groups in the German capital.

“The suspect is known to police. He is known to us as a member of Islamic circles here in Berlin, and our search for this person is proceeding at full speed,” said police spokesman Florian Nath. He did not identify the suspect by name.

Nath added that “we still have no information whatsoever regarding his specific motives, the exact sequence of events, or his role in the crime itself.”

Earlier, police said some of the victims had life-threatening injuries. In a post on X, police called on everyone to leave the site of the event immediately as ambulances and firefighters attended to the victims.

White van hit people in Tiergarten park

According to police, a white van had driven into the Tiergarten park around 10 p.m., which is next to the route that the pride march had passed along earlier, and hit several people before colliding with a tree. Police could not say how many officers had been deployed to the scene but that it was “definitely a lot of police.”

Overall, more than 2,200 police officers have been on duty in Berlin since Saturday morning to protect the pride parade and other LGBTQ+ events in the city.

Police were conducting witness interrogations at the park during the night and were investigating accounts that in addition to the crash some victims appeared to have suffered stab wounds — but that it was too early to draw any conclusion from those accounts.

Berlin Mayor Kai Wegner expressed shock, saying that “following a peaceful and vibrant pride parade, the rally for a tolerant and peaceful Berlin was attacked in the most brutal manner.”

“This is an attack on our free and cosmopolitan society,” Wegner said. “I have confidence in the police and security authorities, who will be working around the clock to investigate.”

Meanwhile, authorities called on possible witnesses to come forward and share with police any video or photos they might have taken at the scene of the attack.

The city also activated a crisis hotline for people missing friends or family members.

Hundreds of thousands of people had come to Berlin on Saturday to celebrate at Berlin’s pride parade, known in Germany as Christopher Street Day. It’s one of Europe’s largest LGBTQ+ celebrations.

Iconic pride event called off

The pride event in front of the city’s Brandenburg Gate, near Tiergarten, was called off around 10:15 p.m. and a band’s performance on stage was interrupted. People were urged to go home and to avoid taking the route through the park.

Before the incident, people had celebrated peacefully, marching through the city for hours, dancing to loud music, and cheering the around 80 floats that participated in the parade.

Julian Miethig, who had attended the LGBTQ+ party at the Brandenburg Gate earlier, said he had just wanted to go to an afterparty when he heard from a friend that “something bad happened there and there are a lot of fire trucks, a lot of emergency vehicles, ambulances.”

He said he went to Tiergarten and was shocked that something like this could have happened at Berlin’s pride celebrations.

“It’s a dark day for the community,” he said.

news_bc.title: BC Football Countdown to Kickoff 2026: Rutgers Preview
news_bc.author: Niraj Patel
news_bc.summary:
Boston College’s home opener will be against Rutgers. The game will feature as Red Bandana Game and will actually be played on the 25th anniversary of 9/11 and Welles Crowther’s passing. The game will be nationally televised on ESPN2.

Last season’s starting quarterback Dylan Lonergan will also make his return with his new team. He started the 2025 season with such promise, but quickly faltered. He’s still in a bit of quarterback competition, but will hope his third stop will see more success.

Game Notes

  • Who: Boston College vs. Rutgers
  • Head Coaches: Bill O’Brien, Boston College; Greg Schiano, Rutgers
  • When: Friday, September 11 at 7:30pm
  • Where: Chestnut Hill, MA

Series History

The Eagle still lead their old Big East compatriots 20-7-1, with 10 wins at home and away. Rutgers did however snap an 11 game winless stretch with the most recent matchup 22-21 at Alumni Stadium to start the 2022 season.

Scarlet Knights 2025 Recap

Schiano’s team took a step back last season, missing out on a bowl game and going 5-7 overall and 2-7 in conference. They took care of business early, but endured some narrow losses to the likes of Iowa, Minnesota, and Penn State that put a damper on the season beyond the expected blowout losses to Oregon and Ohio State. Late-game execution and defensive breakdowns were a constant headache and not typical of a Greg Schiano team. On the positive, the offense was surprisingly explosive and the team finished fifth in the nation in fewest penalty yards. Although quarterback QB Athan Kaliakmanis was drafted in the 7th round, they still return a lot of their most productive offensive players and will try to replicate that output while cleaning up those defensive woes.

Can the offense do it again?

Junior running back Antwan Raymond and 6-6 junior wideout KJ Duff are looked at among the best in the Big Ten. Raymond was the focal point of the ground game, handling the majority of carries running over 5 yards a cli. He finished nearly 1500 yards from scrimmage and a team-leading 15 touchdowns, while being named Second Team All-Conference. Duff joined Raymond on the Second Team, eclipsing 1000 yards as well to go with seven scores. Both find themselves on Preseason All-America lists for the upcoming year. These two will be a real handful.

Overall offense was remarkably efficient, featuring a wide-open passing game, strong red-zone effectiveness from Raymond, and avoided turnovers. The door is open for Dylan Lonergan to take over and keep the ship afloat, but he does appear to still be in a bit of quarterback competition with redshirt sophomore AJ Surace who saw some action last season. The pieces around them are good. The team also returns a few key lineman particularly on the interior, but must replace the tackles. Pass protection left a lot to be desired, so if they can shore that up so Lonergan can keep his much-needed clean pocket, they can replicate some of their success.

Will the defense turn it around?

Schiano will look to restore his defensive reputation after a disappointing campaign in which they were ranked 127th overall. He started by firing nearly the entire defensive staff and brought in South Dakota’s Head Coach Travis Johansen to be his defensive coordinator.

Up front, the team returns most of their interior defensive line and adds a few productive transfers to bolster the rotation. The front saw a fair amount of injuries that made things even more difficult, but among their big issues was getting to the quarterback, posting just 11 sacks with no one even getting to three sacks. Transfers Malachi Davis (Toledo) and J’Dan Burnett (Tulsa) combined for 12 last season. On top of that, the run defense was dismal allowing over 210 yards per game, sixth worst in the FBS and 33 ypg worse than BC. In comes a new tackle and another back from injury, but it will take a lot to clean this up. Most of the key linebackers return and they add in a couple transfers here to make for a really deep corps.

In the secondary, they found three new potential starters in the transfer portal, including an FCS All-American. Last year’s team was porous and only posted 5 interceptions, and they still lost their best corner to Texas. There are still question marks here with all the new faces and a pretty open competition. Schiano’s helped develop some great players over the years, and it won’t take much to get back to their average output from the previous four seasons.

Matchup Preview

Both teams have questions at how their quarterbacks will play, but Rutgers seems to have a lot fewer question marks than BC. With their returning output on offense, they should have the edge early in the season. You have to think Schiano’s defense will make strides, but hopefully the unknown element Mason McKenzie brings to the offense can create more challenges.

The Rutgers loss in 2022 was a harbinger of doom for the Eagles that year. This time we’ll have our feet wet already and won’t have to think ahead with Maine the following week. Rutgers meanwhile starts with UMass but has a date with USC after this one. This being the Red Bandana Game will add an extra energy. The Eagles will pick up their first win of the season here.

news_bc.title: BC Football Countdown to Kickoff 2026: Cincinnati Preview
news_bc.author: Greg Patuto
news_bc.summary:
Boston College is looking to improve off a two-win campaign in 2025.

The Eagles will travel to take on Cincinnati to begin the 2026 season this September.

Game Notes

  • Who: Boston College vs. Cincinnati
  • Head Coaches: Bill O’Brien, Boston College; Scott Satterfield, Cincinnati
  • When: Saturday, September 5 at 3:30pm
  • Where: Nippert Stadium in Cincinnati, Ohio

Series History

These teams have met eight times in their history with the first coming in 1961. They have split these eight meetings, 4-4. Boston College won the first two meetings without allowing a point. Cincinnati got the best of the Eagles in their last game played in 2020.

  • 9/23/1961 – Boston College 23, Cincinnati 0
  • 10/17/1964 – Boston College 10, Cincinnati 0
  • 11/4/1967 – Cincinnati 27, Boston College 21
  • 10/26/1985 – Cincinnati 24, Boston College 17
  • 9/10/1988 – Boston College 41, Cincinnati 7
  • 10/12/1996 – Boston College 24, Cincinnati 17
  • 9/27/1997 – Cincinnati 24, Boston College 6
  • 1/2/2020 – Cincinnati 38, Boston College 6

Cincinnati 2025 Recap

It was a quick start for Cincinnati in 2025. After a season-opening loss to Nebraska, the Bearcats would win seven games in a row including a 5-0 start in Big 12 play. Cincinnati sat at 7-1 with victories over Iowa State, Kansas, and Baylor.

The final third of the season was not kind to Cincinnati. It finished the season with four straight losses against Utah, Arizona, BYU, and TCU. The Bearcats ended the regular season with a record of 7-5 and 5-4 in conference play. Cincinnati was selected for the Autozone Libert Bowl, which was a 35-13 loss to Navy.

Offense: Can new QB continue momentum?

Brendan Sorsby is gone. The former Bearcat was one of the biggest names in the transfer portal before landing at Texas Tech, and whatever else. This means Cincinnati had to hit the portal to land Georgia Southern transfer JC French IV to take over under center.

The question is — can French IV air it out like Sorsby?

Cincinnati moved fast last year and got it done through the air, which led to victories. The Bearcats went 6-0 when averaging ver 8.5 yards per completion. This year, French IV has plenty of wide outs to work with who expect to put up big numbers.

Despite the loss of Cyrus Allen, the Bearcats have an impressive group built through the transfer portal. JV Gibson comes over from Oklahoma along with Larenzo Fenner, Cade Wolford, and Flynn Schele. All are expected to play pivotal roles on the outside.

In the backfield, it’s Zion Johnson who is prepared to break out. French IV is a capable runner as well and this gives the team a dual-threat option.

The other question is — can Cincinnati score against big-time opponents?

The Bearcats got off to that quick start to the season thanks to the offense before being slowed down drastically over the final four games. This is where French IV will have to help the offense take that next step.

Defense: Can it survive being on the field so much?

The flipside to the offense moving quickly is that the defense has to be on the field more. Last year, that hit a wall toward the end of the season and it showed. This year, is the defense prepared for the challenge?

Nate Woody comes in as the defensive coordinator to help fix different issues. Two major transfers on that side of the ball include Chidera Otutu and Josh Hough, who are both expected to make an impact along the defensive line. The Bearcats do not feature that premiere pash rusher so it will need to rely on its depth to get in the backfield.

Another way to offset the speed of the offense is for the defense to get off the field. The Bearcats struggled with this at times, especially when forcing turnovers. Cincinnati came away with just two interceptions on 389 pass attempts by opponents. Cincinnati was also last in the Big 12 in first downs allowed.

Matchup Preview

According to multiple sites, Boston College currently sits as a touchdown underdog in the opener on the road against the Bearcats. While there is a chance that it moves either way before kickoff, that feels about right. It is also not an impossible upset for the Eagles to pull off but it will be an uphill battle. There are many changes on both sides of the ball for both teams but the tempo of Cincinnati can be a bother for opposing defenses. The other angle of this is can Boston College take advantage of some of the Bearcat struggles defensively from last season?

This will ultimately be the decider. Can the Eagles get in the win column early with a statement victory in Week 1?

news_bc.title: Boston College adds pair of special teamers to 2027 class
news_bc.author: Greg Patuto
news_bc.summary:
A duo of special team players out of Florida decided to stick together and come North.

On Friday, kicker Mateo Sanchez and long snapper Aidan Field announced commitments to Boston College. The duo, both from North Broward Prep in Coconut Creek, Florida, visited campus at different times earlier this month before committing.

Sanchez held offers from the likes of Florida State, Duke, and Army. He attended camps at Notre Dame and Georgia Tech as well.

“Thank you to all the coaches who have been with me along this journey, thank you to my parents who have been by my side through all the highs and lows. GO EAGLES!,” Sanchez wrote.

The two sent out posts on the same morning. Field was a Rubio Top 12 invitee this year. The 6-foot-4, 205-pound snapper has a snap time of .68 seconds.

“Thank you to the Boston College coaching staff for this incredible opportunity. I am so grateful to everyone who has supported me along the way, especially my coaches, parents, family, teammates, and friends. I wouldn’t be here without your constant support, encouragement, and belief in me,” Field wrote.

The Eagles now have a total of 29 commits in the Class of 2027. Bill O’Brien has been hitting all aspects of the game in recruiting recently. How do you feel about Boston College’s class next year?

news_bc.title: Boston College Football: Secondary Preview
news_bc.author: Joseph Celia
news_bc.summary:
A pivotal season awaits Boston College Football. The league year is vastly approaching, and it’s going to look a lot different versus last year’s team — to be determined for better or for worse. In regards to 2025-26, one area the team must continue to build on is their secondary. 

Last season, the Eagles allowed the eighth most passing yards in the ACC out of 17 teams. In what was nothing short of a disappointing year, the secondary was one of their few consistent and steady areas on the team. With it being arguably their strongest positional group, they’re retaining a well-established and experienced core that should only improve once the season begins. BC is also bringing in a new DC in Ted Roof, whose defensive schemes rely heavily on zone coverage — another element to watch for. 

The best players in the Eagles secondary group are safeties KP Price and Carter Davis. Both are highly graded in their positional groups. Price returns after leading the team with 93 tackles in 2025 and 2 INT’s. Davis had 59 tackles total and 1 sack. Their cornerbacks group include Max Tucker, Syair Torrence, Isaiah Farris, and Ashton Cunningham. Tucker is only one in this CB group with an INT from last season, but a new defensive scheme can help change that. As for the NB’s, this group includes Cameron Martinez and TJ Green. Roof’s system will benefit them tremendously, as they’ll have a more clear vision of the field to make more plays. 

It’s easy to point to the quarterback and coach as being the keys in achieving in 2026-27 for BC Football. But for the sake of the argument, the team’s secondary could make or break the defense this year, and something that they must continue to build on.

news_bc.title: BC Football Summer Preview: Offensive Line
news_bc.author: Niraj Patel
news_bc.summary:
For the first two seasons of the Bill O’Brien era, the Boston College offensive line was a marriage between old and new: Hafley‑recruited personnel, a holdover position coach, and just enough continuity to keep the Eagles from fully tearing it down up front. Now, Matt Applebaum has moved on and with Kurt Anderson having taken over the room, 2026 is no longer an inheritance and instead in the name, image, and likeness, if you will, of Bill O’Brien.

The Eagles effectively lose four starters on the offensive line, three to the NFL in Bowry (4th Rd), Taylor (6th Rd), Cline (UDFA) and one to transfer (Daugherty), along with a few other rotational guys. Although the unit did struggle in most facets, this is a lot of experience to replace. That means we have a lot of open questions coming into the season and heavy competition.

New offensive coach Kurt Anderson comes in well-regarded from previous coaching spots most notably at Northwestern. He quickly attacked the portal and brought in six transfer lineman to account for only having one starter returning, center Michael Crounse, and one other returner who logged a start in Robert Smith IV.

Starting in the interior, Crounse (R-Jr) anchored the last eight games of the season. He will look to continue his development and should provide a stable base. Yonkers native DJ Williams played in a game last year, maintaining his redshirt, could be the backup here. Smith ended up starting five games across both guard spots and as a true freshman no less. He’s going to stay in the mix regardless of who has been brought in, and his versatility will help him continue to log snaps. Judah Pruitt is the other main returner who spent last year backing up at guard. He got his feet wet in most games, primarily on the kicking units, but could move more into a rotational role. He’s seen some time this offseason at center too.

Kristian Phillips is the first of our transfers. A senior from Michigan State, he was a solid prospect out of high school and flashed that ceiling collegiately, but had his path was knocked off course by injuries. He still managed four starts at right guard last year, but this season feels like a new start for him in a new room and staring at a depth chart that should give him the inside track on locking down a starting role. Owen Snively’s a super-senior who has made 16 career starts between Eastern Michigan and Colorado State (with Daz). The veteran experience will be apt for a plug and play guy, well-suited at left guard where he has more experience, but could flip as needed. I expect the last starting spot to come down to him or Robert Smith, but both should see plenty of work this season at the very least as the extra lineman coming in. Jani Norwood comes to us via the other Bill at UNC. He adds another layer of upside with a hint of experience as a redshirt sophomore. He appeared in six games and started a bowl game as a freshman.

On the tackle front, we have a couple of intriguing prospects. Starting with key returners, redshirt sophomore Pape Abdoulaye Sy returns after serving as Jude Bowry’s backup at left tackle. The 6-7 NFL Academy prospect came in for a bit against Notre Dame and SMU as well.

Trevon Humphrey is jumping up a level from NC Central, but arrives with a heavy workload of 36 starts under his belt in a high scoring offense. He’s a 6-5 upperclassman as is Reggie Jackson from Jacksonville State. Jackson has a strong athletic profile and made 11 starts at right tackle on a top rushing offense. He’s seen some cross-training at guard. Veguer Jean-Jumeau is a redshirt sophomore from Tennessee State. At 6’9 tackle, he was recruited heavily by some other big programs like Miss State and Vandy, so he might have seen BC as the place where he was most likely to get early minutes with a good track record. My guess is the starters will be two of Jackson, Sy, or Humphrey at first, but fully expect to see a few combinations. Given the style of offense under Mason McKenzie, I could see Jackson’s profile giving him the edge.

Amir Johnson is a name to watch among returning players. He transferred in from Merrimack last year where he played left tackle. He was mostly on special teams last year, but could crack the depth chart after a year in the program as a redshirt junior. Souleye Diawara is young, but has a huge frame at 6-9, 340. He was on the special teams unit and played in ten games. The remainder of the crop are freshman we outlined here, but the main callouts would have to be local four-star product Marc Antunes Jr. and Bruno Werner from the NFL Academy.

It might take a bit for this group to really gel with all the new faces and the new coach, and I have a sneaky feeling we’re in for a season where we won’t see the same combination more than a handful of times. There’s a lot of potential here and seemingly good depth, so it’s more a credit to that than a doomsday theory. Still, this feels like the first deliberate build rather than the holdover patch job, albeit with some pretty dang good players.

news_bc.title: Boston College loses major weapon for 2026 season
news_bc.author: Greg Patuto
news_bc.summary:
Boston College will be without one of its biggest offensive weapons for the upcoming season.

On Thursday morning, head coach Bill O’Brien announced that tight end Kaelan Chudzinski will miss the 2026 campaign with an Achilles injury.

Chudzinski was slated to be the team’s starting tight end this season after emerging as one of the nation’s best freshmen at the position in 2025. He totaled 24 catches for 313 yards and four touchdowns in his first season.

With Jeremiah Franklin moving on, this set the stage for Chudzinski to take over as TE1 this season and for the future.

O’Brien shared that he expects Chudzinski to return to football activities in January 2027.

news_bc.title: Boston College Football among toughest schedules in the nation
news_bc.author: Greg Patuto
news_bc.summary:
The Boston College football schedule has been set for months now. Right away, it was clear that the Eagles will be challenged each week.

Boston College is coming off a 2-10 campaign in 2025. The team is looking to improve and to do so, it will have to pick up some hard-fought victories.

Last week, ESPN shared its latest Football Power Index, including strength of schedule of all teams around the nation. In this list, Boston College currently has the 24th hardest schedule in the country this fall.

Boston College Football Schedule

  • Sept. 5: at Cincinnati
  • Sept. 11: vs. Rutgers
  • Sept. 19: vs. Maine
  • Sept. 26: vs. Virginia Tech
  • Oct. 3: at SMU
  • Oct. 17: vs. Pitt
  • Oct. 24: at Georgia Tech
  • Oct. 31: at Duke
  • Nov. 7: vs. Florida State
  • Nov. 14: at Notre Dame
  • Nov. 21: vs. Syracuse
  • Nov. 28: at Miami

The Good

There is a chance that Boston College reaches its win total from last season in Week 3, or maybe even Week 2 if all goes right. For the ultimate optimist out there, is it possible the Eagles double their win total from 2025 by Week 4?

Obviously, no games outside of Maine can be penciled in as a victory. The season opens against Cincinnati before the home opener against Rutgers and a date with Virginia Tech in Week 4. These are three winnable games for the Eagles. In total, Boston College will play five teams that did not play in bowl season last year.

That is the absolute best-case scenario. In reality, Boston College will be a touchdown underdog at least against Cincinnati. The Rutgers game is a massive swing on the schedule before Maine. The minimum goal for the Eagles in the first four should be a split.

The Bad

After those first four games of the season, it does not get easier as Boston College hits the road for three out of four.

A trip to SMU begins October before back-to-back against Georgia Tech and Duke on the road. A home game with Pitt is mixed in. This game is coming off a bye week. The Eagles will have two weeks to prepare for a home game against the Panthers. This is another swing game on the schedule.

Boston College will not play Cal, Clemson, Louisville, North Carolina, NC State, Stanford, Virginia, Wake Forest this year. The Eagles avoid trips out West but Cal and Stanford would have been welcomed. This means the ugly is coming in the ACC.

The Ugly

The final four games of the season will be a gauntlet for the Eagles.

Florida State begins the final third of the year. The Seminoles will come North to play this game but it will be a difficult one for the Eagles. The Eagles will also have a trip to Notre Dame scheduled. The Irish are one of the favorites to win the National Championship this season. Playing this game on the road makes for a massive spread.

Boston College ends the season with a road game against Miami, who finished as the national runner-up last season.

news_bc.title: 5 questions surrounding Boston College entering 2026 ACC Media Days
news_bc.author: Greg Patuto
news_bc.summary:
The ACC is up next on the media days calendar.

The conference will showcase its teams beginning on Wednesday from the Hilton Uptown in Charlotte. Bill O’Brien and Boston College will take the podium on Thursday and there are many burning questions surrounding the Eagles.

Boston College is looking to improve off a 2-10 season in 2025. There are question marks on both sides of the ball on the field along with others off the field to ponder during media days.

1. Can a new offensive line gel right away?

The offensive line struggled in both passing and running situations last season. Even though there were not many losses in the transfer portal, the Eagles knew that they needed to make additions to improve the offensive line.

Boston College brought in guard Kristian Phillips from Michigan State along with tackles Reggie Jackson from Jacksonville State and North Carolina Central’s Trevon Humphrey. It is likely that both Phillips and Jackson will land starting spots along the offensive line. With two new starters and an entire unit that needs to improve, it will be interesting to see how the Eagles perform up front.

2. Mason McKenzie: Will it work?

It was a battle under center for the Eagles but it looks as though the transfer from Saginaw Valley State will come into the season as QB1.

Mason McKenzie committed to Boston College in January and was a contender to start despite his lack of Division I experience, along with Grayson Willson. The book on McKenzie is that he comes to the Eagles with a strong arm and an ability to use his legs. At just 6-foot-1, McKenzie will have to be able to move in the pocket. This fits into what Bill O’Brien likes to do.

The question is — can his game translate to the Division I level and find success right away?

3. Will there be a run game?

The Eagles ranked 15th in the ACC last season with 103.9 rushing yards per game. This was partially because of a disastrous offensive line, but it should be no surprise that the coaching staff went to bring in some new blood. Liberty standout Evan Dickens rushed for 1,339 yards and 16 touchdowns last season. He will now lead the backfield for Boston College, giving the offense an intriguing duo of runners with McKenzie in the mix. The Eagles also loaded up with Nolan Ray transferring in from Maryland. This will be an important part of the offense in order to keep defenses on their toes.

4. Can the defense take the ball away?

This one is self explanatory. The Boston College defense ranked 128th in total last season. Ted Roof came in to be the defensive coordinator and has his hands full but turnovers must be the focal point. Boston College had just six interceptions and six fumbles recovered last season. The team forced 13 fewer turnovers than it did in 2024. The pass rush needs to get better but an experience group in the secondary returns led by KP Price and Carter Davis. The Eagles must find a way to generate more turnovers.

5. Will anyone get to three sacks?

This sounds like a simple feat, right? Wrong.

Boston College was last in the ACC with 17 sacks last season. Sedarius McConnell led the team with 2.5 sacks. That means no Eagle reached the three-sack mark in 12 games played.

The Eagles hit the portal along the defensive line as well in hopes of improving these numbers. Georgia transfer Kris Jones will get the chance to showcase himself after one year in Athens. Harvard transfer Alex DeGrieck and Buffalo transfer Demetrius Ballard also have big-time upside.

US-Russian space crew lands safely after eight-month stint on the ISS

A US-Russian space crew landed safely in the steppes of Kazakhstan on Sunday after an eight-month stint on the International Space Station.

NASA astronaut Chris Williams and Russian crewmates Sergei Kud-Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev touched down in their Soyuz MS-28 that landed smoothly by parachute in a designated area southeast of Dzhezkazgan.
